title: Auto Loans: splitting a catch-up installment payment into fees, interest and principal
content:
# Auto Loans: splitting a catch-up installment payment into fees, interest and principal

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB applies when a borrower pays the earliest past-due installment of an auto loan by a transfer from the borrower's own PCB checking account. It fixes how the payment drawn is divided.

## Clause

The payment is split in the product's application order on the payment amount actually drawn:

1. **Fees portion**: the lesser of the payment amount and the fees due.
2. **Interest portion**: the lesser of the interest owed through the credit date and what remains of the payment amount after the fees portion.
3. **Principal portion**: what remains after the fees portion and the interest portion, rounded to the cent.

Each portion is taken from what the earlier portion left; the three portions together always make up the payment amount.

## Hypothetical cases (fees due 25.00; interest owed 63.16)

| Payment amount drawn | Fees portion | Interest portion | Principal portion |
|---|---|---|---|
| 312.40 | 25.00 | 63.16 | 224.24 |
| 60.00 | 25.00 | 35.00 | 0.00 |
| 20.00 | 20.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |

With no fees due, a payment of 312.40 splits as 0.00, 63.16 and 249.24.

## Points of judgement

**Wrong reading:** "split the full monthly payment." **Correct basis:** the split acts on the payment amount actually drawn, which can be less than the monthly payment.

**Wrong reading:** "interest first, then fees." **Correct basis:** fees come first, then interest, then principal.
